NLD: A pre-salt carbonate reservoir is a subsurface rock unit that is located beneath the Aptian salt layer in the Brazilian offshore basins and capable of storing and producing hydrocarbons. It is primarily composed of lacustrine carbonates, notably microbialites and coquinas. Reservoir quality, including porosity and permeability, is critically controlled by rifting-generated faults and fractures, alongside complex diagenetic alterations.

NLD: A microbialite is a carbonate rock that forms through the in-situ trapping and binding of sediment particles and/or the direct precipitation of minerals by microbial communities. In the Brazilian Pre-Salt, these rocks constitute a major component of the lacustrine reservoirs, often forming intraclasts within re-sedimented deposits.
